about: Tool truth for the Co-Pilot. Generated from src/ai/flows/ogeemo-chat.ts and src/lib/command-processor.ts - document ONLY what exists. Enforced by tests/knowledge-base.test.ts; update in the same commit as agent changes.

tools.name: syncReceipts
tools.description: Lists PDF files in the Google Drive "Receipts" folder, when Drive is connected.
tools.sideEffects: Read-only. Google Drive is not connected yet, so it returns an empty list and says so; point the user to Receipt Intake (/accounting/receipt-processor).

tools.name: searchContacts
tools.description: Searches the workspace's contacts by name, company, email or phone number and returns their ids.

inputs.searchTerm: string - name, company, email or phone fragment (every word must match)

tools.sideEffects: Read-only (Firestore contacts, scoped to the user's workspace). At most 20 results are returned.
tools.auth: Requires a signed-in user inside a workspace; the workspace comes from the server session.

tools.name: searchGlobal
tools.description: Searches Ogeemo pages and the workspace's contacts and projects by name, and returns real record ids.
tools.sideEffects: Read-only search; no writes, no web search. It never invents people.
tools.auth: Pages are searched for everyone; contacts and projects only for a signed-in user, inside their own workspace.

tools.name: createContact
tools.description: Adds a contact to the workspace's Contacts Hub and saves it.

inputs.name: string (required, at least 2 characters)
inputs.folder: string (optional) - a contact folder name in this workspace; the default folder is used when omitted
inputs.email: string (optional, must look like an email address)
inputs.allowDuplicate: boolean (optional) - true only after the user said to add it although a similar contact exists

tools.sideEffects: WRITES a document to the Firestore 'contacts' collection, stamped with the workspace, the creator and search keywords, exactly as the Contacts Hub does. It refuses a contact with the same email address or the same name as an existing one (nothing is written) until allowDuplicate is true. It never adds Employees or Contractors (those need pay and document setup: use the Workers page, /workers) and never accepts a SIN, pay rate or employment dates. If the database is unavailable nothing is written and the reply says the contact was NOT added.
tools.auth: Requires a signed-in user in a workspace with the editor, org_admin or super_admin role; a viewer is refused.

tools.name: createAppointment
tools.description: Books an appointment on the signed-in user's Calendar and saves it.

inputs.title: string (required)
inputs.startTime: ISO date-time WITH a time of day (required; without an offset it is read in the user's time zone; a date alone is refused)
inputs.endTime: ISO date-time (optional) - use this or durationMinutes
inputs.durationMinutes: number 5 to 720 (optional; one hour when neither length is given)
inputs.contactId: string (optional) - must be a contact in this workspace, from searchContacts
inputs.allowDoubleBooking: boolean (optional) - true only after the user said to book it although it overlaps something

tools.sideEffects: WRITES a document to the Firestore 'tasks' collection with activityType 'appointment', scheduled, stamped with the workspace and the person who asked, so it shows on the Calendar and is never flagged overdue. Planned time only: it is never worked or billable time. It refuses a time in the past, an end before the start, and a length over 12 hours. It refuses a time that overlaps one of the user's OWN unfinished timed events (nothing is written), names the clash and suggests the next free time inside 9:00 to 17:00 in the user's time zone, until allowDoubleBooking is true. If the database is unavailable nothing is written and the reply says the appointment was NOT booked.
tools.auth: Requires a signed-in user in a workspace with the editor, org_admin or super_admin role; a viewer is refused.

tools.name: getCalendar
tools.description: Reads the signed-in user's own Calendar for one day or up to 14 days.

inputs.date: YYYY-MM-DD (optional; today in the user's time zone when omitted)

tools.sideEffects: Read-only (Firestore tasks, scoped to the user's workspace). Returns up to 30 of the user's own scheduled events with the time written in their time zone. It never shows other people's events.
tools.auth: Requires a signed-in user inside a workspace; the workspace comes from the server session.

tools.name: createTask
tools.description: Creates a task in the Activity Manager: a to-do, or a scheduled task. For an appointment, meeting or call at a set time, use createAppointment instead.

inputs.title: string (required)
inputs.startTime: ISO date-time (optional; presence makes it a scheduled event; without an offset it is read in the user's time zone)
inputs.endTime: ISO date-time (optional; one hour after the start when omitted)
inputs.contactId: string (optional) - must be a contact in this workspace, from searchContacts
inputs.projectId: string (optional) - must be a project in this workspace; the task also becomes a step of the project

tools.sideEffects: WRITES a document to the Firestore 'tasks' collection with status 'todo', stamped with the workspace so the app lists it. A task with no date and no project is a To-Do List item. If the database is unavailable nothing is written and the reply says the task was NOT created.
tools.auth: Requires a signed-in user in a workspace with the editor, org_admin or super_admin role; a viewer is refused.

flows.name: contactCapability
flows.description: Structured contact form flow, used to edit an existing contact, to fill a New Contact form the user has already opened, and to explain how to add a contact. Asking Co-Pilot to ADD a contact is handled by the createContact tool, which saves it directly. Never choose tenant/audit/folder IDs for the user. Confidential HR fields (SIN, pay rate) require explicit consent because chat history is retained.
flows.sideEffects: UI-assisted: it prepares forms and navigation, and for an edit it asks the open form to save. The form remains the place that validates the save.

commands.how: The command processor maps normalized natural-language words to navigation and simple actions (src/lib/command-processor.ts). Examples:

examples.say: timer, start timer, log time, track time

examples.does: opens the income or expenses tab of the ledger

cannotYet: Query business data: time logs, unbilled totals, invoice lists and payroll runs cannot be read by tools yet - point the user to the relevant report/screen from 03_operational_qna.md. The user's own Calendar CAN be read with getCalendar.

Create or edit invoices, quotes, receipts or payroll directly as writes. Adding a contact is possible (createContact), but editing an existing contact is UI-assisted via the contactCapability flow, and Employees and Contractors are added on the Workers page (/workers).
Send emails, notifications or file changes; manage users, tenants or settings.

Modify, move, cancel or delete existing tasks, events or appointments (createTask and createAppointment only create); point the user to the Calendar (/calendar), where an event can be dragged or deleted. Invite or notify other people, or see anyone else's calendar.
